Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write a monthly engineering update for a team of twelve, covering a migration, two hires, and a slipped deadline. Around 200 words.

# Engineering update — August

The Postgres migration is done. We cut over on the 19th with 40 minutes of read-only time, under the two-hour window we'd announced. Two things surprised us. The connection pooler needed retuning under real load, and three reporting queries that ran fine on the old planner had to be rewritten. Both are fixed. Nothing rolled back.

Priya joined the platform team on the 4th and has already shipped the pooler retune above. Marcus starts on the 15th of September on billing; his onboarding buddy is Jen, and the first-week plan is in the team drive.

The checkout rewrite has slipped from September 12th to October 3rd. We caused that ourselves by scoping it before the migration was finished and underestimating how much of the payment path touched the old schema. I'd rather say that plainly than blame the migration. Sales and support have the new date, and I've asked Dana to run a scoping review before we commit to the next multi-sprint project. She'll start with the estimates we got wrong here, since those are the ones we can still check against reality.

Headcount is twelve as of the 15th. That is the largest this team has been, and it changes how we review — expect a proposal on splitting the on-call rotation in the next two weeks.

The deadline slipped again. Update it and explain why.

# Engineering update — September

The checkout rewrite has moved again, from October 3rd to November 14th. That is the second slip, and the cause is different from the first.

In August I said we underestimated how much of the payment path touched the old schema. That was true and we fixed it. What we did not do was check the same assumption against the refund and chargeback flows, which sit behind a service we do not own. Those flows read three columns we dropped in the migration. The team that owns that service can pick up the work in their next cycle, which starts October 20th. We can either wait or write a compatibility shim we throw away in December. I have chosen to wait, because the shim is two weeks of work that leaves us with a second code path in billing.

The scoping review Dana ran caught the payment path. It did not cover services outside our repo, so I am extending it: any project that crosses a team boundary now needs a named owner on the other side before we set a date. Marcus is drafting that with Dana.

Sales and support have November 14th. I am not going to say it is firm, since I said that twice already. It is the date we believe with what we know now.
